plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double flowers held above deep green, lobed foliage. It is a beloved cut flower and garden staple that thrives in cool-winter climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies can live for more than 100 years, and ants visiting the flower buds feed on nectar but are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: A tough, thorny deciduous shrub with wrinkled, leathery leaves and fragrant single or semi-double flowers, followed by large, edible orange-red hips rich in vitamin C. It tolerates salt spray and sandy soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer, with peak bloom in early June
plants.location: Native to coastal East Asia (northern China, Japan, Korea); naturalized along North Atlantic and Baltic coasts
plants.funFact: Rosa rugosa is considered invasive in parts of Europe and New England because its suckering roots form dense coastal thickets.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen subshrub with silvery-gray, narrow leaves and spikes of fragrant purple flowers that attract bees and butterflies. Mediterranean-type climates with well-drained soil suit it best.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid summer (June to August), beginning in early June in warmer areas
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria and the Pacific Northwest of the US
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, fern-leaved, semi-deciduous tree that produces dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting streets and lawns with purple petals when they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); September to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Southern California, Florida, Mexico, South Africa, Australia and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, the jacaranda is so abundant it is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', and in Mexico and parts of the US, falling blossoms are said to bring good luck.
